context.decisions:
architect: Build a Web App named Peer Gate Notes for a learner collecting plain text notes. The accepted scope is the following complete list:
1. A Home page headed Peer Gate Notes.
2. A note form with a required Title field; trim input and reject blank titles.
3. List the saved title and its slug in insertion order, in memory only; reload clears entered notes.
4. Use the real npm package slugify@1.6.6, dynamically imported when saving, to generate a lowercase URL-safe slug from each Title while preserving the original Title.
5. An About page explaining the in-memory data behavior.
6. Home/About navigation.
7. Ten separate onboarding text components, all visible on Home, with these exact labels and useful instructions: Purpose; Add a title; Save a note; Read your list; Understand the slug; Visit About; Return Home; Reload behavior; Plain text safety; Keep learning.
8. Generate a complete working app with its dependency manifest, lockfile and executable tests. No authentication, backend, persistent note storage, editing or deletion is requested. Use the current supported deterministic Web App profile and the smallest compatible catalog architecture. These choices are settled; provide the starting architecture when ready, without optional feature questions.

objects.text: Peer Gate Notes: Welcome to your learner workspace for collecting plain text notes and practicing title-to-slug creation in memory.
Purpose: This app helps learners collect plain text notes in one simple place to practice creating titles and understanding how web apps handle in-memory data without complexity.
Add a title: Type your note title into the required Title field. The form automatically trims whitespace and will reject blank titles so every note has meaningful content.
Save a note: Press Save to store your entry. On save the app dynamically imports slugify@1.6.6 to generate a lowercase URL-safe slug while preserving your original Title exactly as typed.
Read your list: Saved notes appear below the form in insertion order, each showing the original Title alongside its generated slug for easy review and comparison.
Understand the slug: The slug is a lowercase, URL-friendly version of your Title created by slugify, keeping the original Title unchanged for display while providing a web-safe identifier.
Visit About: Click the About link in the navigation to learn how in-memory storage works and why your notes exist only for the current session.
Return Home: Use the Home link to return to the main page from About and continue adding new titles where your list and form await.
Reload behavior: Because notes are stored in memory only, reloading the page clears all entered notes and gives you a fresh empty list to start again.
Plain text safety: Only plain text titles are stored, with no rich text or formatting, keeping entries safe, simple, and free from authentication or backend risks.
Keep learning: Keep adding titles and observing slugs to build intuition for web fundamentals, knowing this practice space has no persistent storage, editing, or deletion to manage.

About in-memory behavior: Notes are stored in memory only and reload clears entered notes. There is no backend, authentication, or persistent storage — your titles and slugs exist only until you refresh, making this a safe learning sandbox for plain text practice.

# Generated application

Run npm install, npm test, npm run build, then npm run dev.

Form data lives in memory for this first generation profile; reloading clears changes. API services expose GET JSON calls; a backend is not generated. Source assembly does not certify governance approval. Review the generated project before execution.
